description: Each year HUD receives custom tabulations of American Community Survey data from the U.S. Census Bureau, known as the CHAS data (Comprehensive Housing Affordability Strategy), which show the extent of housing problems and housing needs, especially for low-income households. Local governments use them to plan the spending of HUD funds, and HUD may use them to distribute grants. The tables count households by income, tenure and race or ethnicity against four housing problems and four severe housing problems, including cost burden. The latest release, on 23 December 2025, is based on 2018-2022 ACS five-year estimates, and the download tool holds every release from 2006-2008 onward for several geographic summary levels; older CHAS from the 2000 census and the 2005-2007 ACS are separate. Format and access: a web query tool, a bulk download page and an API that needs a free account and access token. Licence: not stated on the pages read. Caveats: Census disclosure avoidance suppresses some estimates since the 2018 tables, some categories were merged or suppressed, variable names changed from earlier releases, and the page itself warns about year-to-year comparisons. Simulation uses: household vulnerability and housing need layers for equity weighting in infrastructure and disaster planning. Related records: the American Housing Survey and the US Census ACS commuting flows.
